subject: elephant
readings: head at -x: XY panel is the profile (side view); ZY panel is the FRONT view (facing the trunk/tusks, ears spread left-right); XZ panel is the TOP view.
XY panel: withers (9,4), rump (17,4) -> back is nearly level, torso spans x=9..17
XY panel: neck_base (6,5), head (3,6) -> head sits slightly below withers, forward of body
XY panel: front shoulder (9,8), front knee (9,14), front foot (9,19) -> ground at y~19
XY panel: hind hip (17,8), hind knee (17,14), hind foot (17,19) -> matches front leg length
XY panel: tail_base (21,10), tail_tip (23,16) -> long thin tail hanging down-back
XY panel: trunk_mid (3,9), trunk_tip (7,17) -> trunk curls down and slightly forward, tip near ground
XY panel: ear tip visible ~(5,6), flap folded over back of head
ZY panel: ear tips at z=7 (right side, near screen-left) and z=18 (left side, near screen-right)
ZY panel: leg column at z=9 (right legs) and z=16 (left legs), body center z~12-13
ZY panel: trunk hanging centrally z~15, y=8..16; small tail shadow z~13, y=16..20
Facing direction -x with up +y gives animal-right = -z, animal-left = +z (right-hand rule), used to assign _L/_R from ZY z-values
notes: Head (fused with neck) is kept as an internal spine node rather than a leaf because it bears further terminal appendages (ears, trunk); only those distal flaps count as leaves, per the sub-flap rule applied to the head's own attachments. Leg chains were split into a proximal 'shoulder/hip' offset segment (scapula/pelvis bulge, inferred from where the leg silhouette departs from the torso outline) plus a knee joint and foot, a 3-segment simplification of thigh-knee-shank-foot since the mesh doesn't show a distinct hock. Neck was split into neck_base/head since withers (9,4) and head (3,6) differ in both x and y, ruling out a vertical neck. Trunk was split into a short base curve and a long tip since it visibly bends partway down in the XY panel. Left/right assignment used the ZY (front) panel z-values combined with the head-at -x facing direction and the right-hand rule (forward x up = right), giving animal-right at smaller z and animal-left at larger z; all four legs share the same z pairing since front/hind stance widths look equal.
